2025_329_tsd_administration_building_cat.paragraph: Quote 1461.001 from ISCG (Interior Systems Contract Group Inc.) of Royal Oak, Michigan, printed September 25, 2025, prices BuzziSpace lounge seating and installation for the Troy School District administration building at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 under Project 1461. The quote covers three BuzziSpace poufs, a Haworth tariff surcharge, and receiving/delivery/installation labor priced per the State of Michigan MiDeal seating contract #240000000497, for a total of $1,807.25 with no tax and a required deposit of $722.90. Terms are 50% deposit with the balance net 30, and ISCG's twenty standard terms and conditions are attached.

2025_330_2_g_bond_resolution_sbqlp_troy_.paragraph: A resolution of the Troy School District Board of Education, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, authorizes issuance of 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $220,000,000, combining the second series of new-money bonds under the November 8, 2022 bond proposal with a current refunding of the district's 2016 School Building and Site Bonds. Of that total, the portion for projects and associated issuance costs may not exceed $193,000,000; if net present value savings on the refunding fall below 3.00% of the principal of the Refunded Bonds, the district may issue only the $193,000,000 project portion. The resolution appoints Huntington Securities, Inc. as senior managing underwriter, Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. as bond counsel, and PFM Financial Advisors LLC as municipal advisor, and caps true interest cost at 5.50% per annum.
2025_330_2_g_bond_resolution_sbqlp_troy_.page:
**Instrument**
Resolution Authorizing 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan. Recited as adopted at a regular meeting of the Board of Education held in the School District on November 18, 2025, at 7:00 p.m. local time, with Present/Absent, mover, supporter, AYES and NAYS lines left blank. Certified by Emina Alic, Secretary, Board of Education, including an Open Meetings Act (Act 267, Public Acts of 1976) compliance certification. Document reference 44944687.

**Background recitals**

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| 2022 Bond Proposal approved | General School Election, November 8, 2022 |
| Authorization ceiling | not to exceed $555,000,000 |
| First series (2023 Bonds) | 2023 School Building and Site Bonds, dated March 7, 2023 |
| 2023 Bonds principal | $171,370,000 |
| 2023 net original issue premium | $18,629,212.85, counted against the $555,000,000 authorization |
| Prior Bonds | 2016 School Building and Site Bonds, dated December 28, 2016 |
| Refunded Bonds | Prior Bonds maturing May 1, 2027 through May 1, 2032, inclusive |

The 2022 proposal purposes include remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities; erecting and completing, equipping and furnishing a replacement middle school and classroom additions; acquiring and installing instructional technology infrastructure and equipment; acquiring, preparing, developing and improving sites; and the purchase of school buses.

**Authorization and parameters**

| Parameter | Limit |
|---|---|
| Aggregate principal, combined issue | not to exceed $220,000,000 |
| New money (Projects) portion | not to exceed $193,000,000 |
| Minimum NPV refunding savings | 3.00% |
| True interest cost | not exceeding 5.50% per annum |
| Underwriter's discount | not exceeding 0.75% of principal |
| Final maturity | not later than 30 years from date of issue |
| Denomination | $5,000 or integral multiples |
| Maturity dates | May 1 and/or November 1 |
| Interest payment dates | semiannually, May 1 and November 1 |
| Record date | fifteenth day of the month prior to payment date |

If issued solely for projects, the bonds are designated "2026 School Building and Site Bonds." Bonds may be issued in book-entry-only form through The Depository Trust Company, New York, New York, as serial or term bonds, subject to optional or mandatory redemption as determined by the Authorized Officer.

**Funds established**
Debt Retirement Fund (2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds Debt Retirement Fund) unless a Common Debt Retirement Fund is used; Capital Projects Fund (2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds Projects Fund); Cost of Issuance Fund; and an Escrow Fund held by an Escrow Agent under an Escrow Agreement, invested in direct or guaranteed United States obligations sufficient without reinvestment to pay the Refunded Bonds.

**Tax pledge**
Commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, the district must levy annually an amount sufficient to pay principal and interest, without limitation as to rate or amount, under Article IX, Sections 6 and 16 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963.

**Professionals**
Senior managing underwriter: Huntington Securities, Inc. Bond counsel: Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. Municipal advisor: PFM Financial Advisors LLC. The Superintendent and the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, either acting individually, serve as Authorized Officer.

**Statutory and regulatory framework**
Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001 (including Section 315(1)(d)); Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976; the School Bond Qualification, Approval, and Loan Act, Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005; SEC Rule 15c2-12; and Treas. Reg. § 1.150-2 reimbursement declarations, with maximum debt expected for the Projects stated as $193,000,000.

**Exhibits**
Exhibit A, bond form (Registered Owner Cede & Co.); Exhibit B, Continuing Disclosure Undertaking; Exhibit C, form of Application for Final Qualification of Bonds.
2025_330_2_g_bond_resolution_sbqlp_troy_.verbose:
Title and setting: TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT, COUNTY OF OAKLAND, State of MICHIGAN, RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds (UNLIMITED TAX GENERAL OBLIGATION). The resolution recites a regular meeting of the Board of Education held in the School District on November 18, 2025, at 7:00 p.m., local time. The PRESENT and ABSENT member lines, the names of the offering and supporting members, and the AYES and NAYS lines are blank in this draft. RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED is followed by signature blocks for Emina Alic, Secretary, Board of Education, including a certification that the foregoing is a true and complete copy of a resolution adopted at a regular meeting held on November 18, 2025, conducted with public notice given in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of 1976, as amended. The document bears the reference number 44944687.

Recitals. At the General School Election held November 8, 2022, the qualified electors approved issuance of bonds, in one or more series, in an amount not to exceed $555,000,000 (the 2022 Bond Proposal), for remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities; erecting and completing, equipping and furnishing a replacement middle school and classroom additions and other additions to existing school buildings and other facilities; acquiring and installing instructional technology infrastructure and equipment; and acquiring Sites, preparing, developing and improving Sites, and the purchase of school buses (the Projects). Under Section 6, Article IX and Section 16, Article IX of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, the tax levies for those bonds are without limitation as to rate or amount. The School District previously issued its 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), dated March 7, 2023, in the original principal amount of $171,370,000, as the first series under the 2022 Bond Proposal. Due to prevailing market conditions at sale, the 2023 Bonds were issued with net original issue premium of $18,629,212.85, which is counted against the $555,000,000 authorization. The Board desires to authorize a second series in an aggregate principal amount of not to exceed $193,000,000. Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, permits refunding of funded indebtedness. The School District previously issued its 2016 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), dated December 28, 2016 (the Prior Bonds), and the Board determines it is in the best interest of the district to currently refund all or a portion of the Prior Bonds maturing May 1, 2027 through May 1, 2032, inclusive (the Refunded Bonds). Because the source of payment is the same and to reduce issuance and administration cost, the Board combines the new money and refunding issues into a single series in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $220,000,000, while maintaining a separate capital projects fund for the Projects. If market interest rates rise so that refunding becomes noneconomic or inefficient, the Board retains the option of issuing only not to exceed $193,000,000 for the Projects. The district will sell the bonds by negotiated sale, and authorizes the Superintendent and the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, either acting individually (the Authorized Officer), to accept a purchase offer, negotiate, approve and execute a bond purchase agreement, and approve other terms and documents. The district must be granted qualified status under Act 34 or receive prior approval from the Michigan Department of Treasury.

Issuance of Bonds. The Bonds are designated 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), issuable in one or more series with appropriate name, designation or suffix changes, in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $220,000,000 or such lesser amount as determined by the Authorized Officer, to finance a portion of the Projects, refund the Refunded Bonds, and pay costs of issuance. The portion issued for the Projects and associated issuance costs shall not exceed $193,000,000, with the balance used to refund the Refunded Bonds. If the Authorized Officer, on advice of the Municipal Advisor, determines that net present value savings from refinancing the Refunded Bonds is not at least 3.00% of the principal of the Refunded Bonds, the district may issue not to exceed $193,000,000 for Projects and issuance costs only, in which case the bonds are designated "2026 School Building and Site Bonds" and conforming changes are made to Exhibit A, the Debt Retirement Fund name and purpose, and the application of proceeds.

Bond Details. Bonds are registered as to principal and interest, in denominations of $5,000 or integral multiples, dated as of the date of delivery or another date set by the Authorized Officer, and numbered as determined by the Transfer Agent. Maturities fall on May 1 and/or November 1 in years and amounts set at sale, with final maturity not later than thirty (30) years from the date of issue. Interest rates are set upon negotiated sale, not exceeding a true interest cost of 5.50% per annum, payable semiannually on May 1 and November 1. The underwriter's discount shall not exceed 0.75% of the principal amount. Principal is payable at a bank or trust company selected by the Authorized Officer as registrar and transfer agent; interest is payable by check drawn on the Transfer Agent mailed to the registered owner of record as of the fifteenth day of the month prior to each payment date, subject to future change to conform to market practice. The Bonds may be issued in book-entry-only form through The Depository Trust Company in New York, New York, as serial or term bonds or both, subject to optional or mandatory redemption at times, manner and prices determined by the Authorized Officer. Official notice of redemption by the Transfer Agent must state at minimum the original issue date, maturity dates, interest rates, CUSIP numbers if any, certificate numbers and called amounts, redemption date, redemption price, the place of surrender, and that interest ceases to accrue after the redemption date.

Execution. The Bonds shall be substantially in the form of Exhibit A, signed by manual or facsimile signatures of the President and Secretary of the Board, and are not valid until authenticated by the Transfer Agent, which delivers them to the purchaser per instructions from the Treasurer of the Board upon payment.

Funds. Unless a Common Debt Retirement Fund is established, the Treasurer opens a special depositary account designated 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds Debt Retirement Fund, receiving all tax proceeds levied for principal, interest and redemption price, plus any accrued interest received on delivery. A Capital Projects Fund designated the 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds Projects Fund receives amounts specified by the Authorized Officer from net sale proceeds and net original issue premium, used solely for Project costs and, as necessary, rebate of arbitrage earnings to the United States Department of Treasury under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. Issuance costs go to a separate 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds Cost of Issuance Fund, with remaining moneys allocated between the Capital Projects Fund and the Debt Retirement Fund on the advice of Bond Counsel. Moneys remaining after Project completion may be used first for any purpose permitted by the 2022 Bond Proposal and second for any other purpose permitted by law. Net original issue premium related to the new money portion is counted against the 2022 Bond Proposal authorization. An Escrow Fund, funded from the balance of Bond proceeds plus any moneys transferred from the Prior Bonds' debt retirement funds and other available funds, is held as cash or invested in direct obligations of, or obligations unconditionally guaranteed by, the United States of America, held by an Escrow Agent under an Escrow Agreement that irrevocably directs a call for redemption of the specified Prior Bonds, with investments sufficient without reinvestment to pay principal and interest on the Refunded Bonds.

Unlimited Tax. Commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, the district must levy a tax annually sufficient to pay principal and interest when due, without limitation as to rate or amount.

Sale and professionals. Having weighed competitive versus negotiated sale under Act 34 and on the advice of the Municipal Advisor, the Board determines a negotiated sale gives greater flexibility in structuring maturities and timing. Huntington Securities, Inc. is appointed senior managing underwriter; the Authorized Officer may appoint co-managing underwriters if recommended by the Municipal Advisor, and may execute the bond purchase agreement without further Board approval subject to the parameters: true interest cost not exceeding 5.50% per annum, net present value savings not less than 3.00% of the projected debt service on the Refunded Bonds absent refunding based on Treasury guidelines, and underwriter's discount not exceeding 0.75% of principal. The Authorized Officer may execute a sale order evidencing final terms. The law firm of Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. is appointed Bond Counsel, with its periodic representation in unrelated matters of Huntington Securities, Inc. and other potential parties expressly approved. PFM Financial Advisors LLC is appointed Municipal Advisor. The Authorized Officer may apply for bond ratings and purchase municipal bond insurance if deemed appropriate; the President of the Board and the Authorized Officer may each approve preliminary and final official statements and execute the final Official Statement and any amendments.

Disclosure, tax and reimbursement. The district covenants under Rule 15c2-12 to provide the information in Exhibit B. It covenants to maintain the exclusion of interest from adjusted gross income for federal income tax purposes under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. Reimbursement declarations under Treas. Reg. § 1.150-2 state the district expects to reimburse itself from debt proceeds for Project expenditures paid subsequent to sixty (60) days prior to the resolution date; the maximum principal amount of debt expected to be issued for the Projects, including issuance costs, is $193,000,000; the reimbursement allocation will occur not later than 18 months after the later of payment or placement in service or abandonment, and in no event more than three (3) years after the original expenditure; expenditures are capital expenditures as defined in Treas. Reg. § 1.1.150-1(b); and no proceeds will be used in a manner described in Treas. Reg. § 1.150-2(h), including creating replacement proceeds within Treas. Reg. § 1.148-1 within one year of the reimbursement allocation. The Authorized Officer may adjust final bond details under Section 315(1)(d) of Act 34, may apply to Treasury for prior approval or file a qualifying statement, may request waivers including rating waivers, and may file a Security Report. Officers may submit a request for interim approval and other actions for qualification under the School Bond Qualification, Approval, and Loan Act, Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005; the Authorized Officer may approve the Application for Final Qualification in substantially the form of Exhibit C and sign loan agreements, and the Secretary of the Board is directed to execute and submit the completed Application. All conflicting resolutions are rescinded.

Exhibit A, Bond Form. United States of America, State of Michigan, County of Oakland, Troy School District, 2026 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation). Registered Owner: Cede & Co. Interest is computed on the basis of a 360-day year consisting of twelve 30-day months. The bonds are issued under Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, as amended, and Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, pursuant to the resolution adopted November 18, 2025, as the second series authorized by the November 8, 2022 election and to refund a portion of an outstanding issue. The full faith and credit of the School District is irrevocably pledged. Transfer agent designation may be changed on notice mailed not less than 60 days prior to an interest payment date. Notice of redemption is given at least 30 days and not more than 60 days prior to the redemption date; bonds are called in multiples of $5,000, and denominations greater than $5,000 are treated as the number of bonds obtained by dividing by $5,000. The Transfer Agent need not register a transfer or exchange during the period beginning 15 days before mailing of a redemption notice and ending at the close of business on the day of mailing. The bond form includes blanks for Interest Rate, Maturity Date, Date of Original Issue, and CUSIP, a Certificate of Authentication with Date of Authentication in 2026, and signature blocks for the President and Secretary.

Exhibit B, Form of Continuing Disclosure Undertaking. Definitions cover Audited Financial Statements (annual audited statements prepared by independent certified public accountants as required by Act 2, Public Acts of Michigan, 1968, as amended), Bondholders, EMMA (the MSRB's Electronic Municipal Market Access system), Financial Obligation, MSRB, Rule, and SEC. The district agrees to provide to the MSRB through EMMA, on or before the last day of the 6th month after the end of its fiscal year, commencing with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026, annual financial information and operating data similar to Official Statement tables covering: Enrollment - Historical Enrollment; State Aid Payments; Property Valuations - History of Valuations; Major Taxpayers; School District Tax Rates (per $1,000 of Valuation); Tax Levies and Collections; Retirement Plan - Contribution to MPSERS; Debt Statement - Direct Debt; School Loan Revolving Fund (SLRF) Program; and General Fund Budget Summary, current year only, in Appendix C. Audited Financial Statements are filed when available, with unaudited statements filed by the deadline if necessary. Notice of failure to disclose must be timely. Sixteen listed events must be reported within ten business days, including principal and interest payment delinquencies; non-payment related defaults, if material; unscheduled draws on debt service reserves or credit enhancements reflecting financial difficulties; substitution or failure of credit or liquidity providers; adverse tax opinions, IRS proposed or final determinations of taxability, Notices of Proposed Issue (IRS Form 5701-TEB); modifications to holder rights, if material; bond calls, if material, and tender offers; defeasances; release, substitution, or sale of property securing repayment, if material; rating changes; bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership or similar event; consummation of a merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, if material; appointment of a successor or additional trustee or trustee name change, if material; incurrence of a material Financial Obligation or agreement to covenants, events of default, remedies, priority rights or similar terms affecting security holders, if material; and default, event of acceleration, termination event, or modification of terms under a Financial Obligation reflecting financial difficulties. Materiality is determined under federal securities laws. Reporting terminates when the district is no longer an obligated person, including upon legal defeasance. The undertaking benefits Bondholders and is enforceable only by specific enforcement, with noncompliance not constituting a default on the Bonds. Amendment provisions track SEC interpretations, including comparison of financial statements if accounting principles change, with notice sent to the MSRB through EMMA. Exhibit C is the Form of Application for Final Qualification of Bonds.
